summary: Evaluates animation/state flag bytes to decide whether a stored-state comparison runs, then always dispatches a callback and returns whether the current state bytes differ from the stored value. A local gate v2 starts at 1; it is cleared to 0 only when the flag path selected by control byte this+0x10C bit 0x20 satisfies its condition (either this+0x5C holds the full 0x300 mask, or this+0x5D has bit 0x8 set). CallbackDispatchWithNullGuard is invoked unconditionally, after which the function returns v2 AND (ByteArrayToInt of the argument-slot bytes != this+0x100).

operations.description: Guard: control flags byte (this+0x10C) bit 0x20 selects the primary flag path; when clear, the alternate flag path (this+0x5D) is evaluated instead.
Guard: when control bit 0x20 is set, the flags register (this+0x5C) must have both bits of the 0x300 mask set; otherwise execution jumps past the gate-clear and v2 stays 1.
Guard: when control bit 0x20 is clear, the low byte (this+0x5D) must have bit 0x8 set; if clear, execution jumps past the gate-clear and v2 stays 1.

Gate decision: v2 is cleared to 0 (disabling the state-change comparison) only when the active flag path passes its guard, i.e. (this+0x10C bit 0x20 set AND this+0x5C has the 0x300 mask) OR (bit clear AND this+0x5D has bit 0x8).
Unconditional dispatch: call CallbackDispatchWithNullGuard(a1, (int)&a1, 4), passing the object pointer, the address of the parameter slot, and the value 4.

Return v2 AND (ByteArrayToInt over the four bytes of the a1 argument slot != stored value this+0x100), i.e. report a state change only when the gate is enabled and the assembled byte value differs from the stored value.

unresolved: Both (int)&a1 arguments are the stack address of the parameter slot, so the four bytes assembled by ByteArrayToInt equal the pointer value a1 itself; whether the intended input is the pointer value or a decompiler artifact is unconfirmed.
The exact semantics of the flag bits (this+0x10C bit 0x20, the two bits covered by the this+0x5C 0x300 mask, and this+0x5D bit 0x8) are not established.
this+0x100 is described in the existing analysis as a stored CRC32 accumulator, but its write site and computation are outside this function.
The object owner is unknown; the field layout between offsets 0x5C and 0x10C is unconfirmed.
